features.rationale: Turn the solid body, spigots, centered circumferential groove and right body chamfer. The disputed left end bevel is deferred.
features.justification: The .062 CENT. groove is symmetric about the line .250 left of the main shoulder, with the depicted 1.188 root diameter. The factor 1.7320508075688772 is cotangent of the printed 30-degree flank angle D009, giving the axial flank run from the radial rise; it is not an independently assumed dimension. The printed 45-degree chamfer D012 has equal axial and radial components.

features.rationale: Apply the specified concave right shoulder radius.
Model the centered tapped region with a standard tap-drill cylinder and cosmetic thread.
features.justification: A #21 drill, .159 inch diameter, is the standard cutting-tap drill for #10-32 UNF from standard Unified thread tap-drill charts. The end view centers the hole on the axis. D018 controls the threaded length only; additional drilling allowance remains unresolved.

features.rationale: What total full-diameter tap-drill depth is required beyond the .38 tapped length?
features.justification: The .159 diameter is the standard #21 tap drill for #10-32 UNF. No separate total drilling depth is specified. The drill point is cosmetic.

features.rationale: Does .094 specify the axial bevel extent at 30 degrees, or must the end-tip diameter also equal 1.188? Those requirements yield different bevels.
features.justification: The parameters identify disputed printed requirements, not an approved chamfer. Leave the end square pending clarification.

features.rationale: What nominal left shoulder radius should be modeled within the specified maximum?
features.justification: D010 is an upper bound, not a specified nominal radius.

notes: Origin is the center of the left end face; +Z points toward the tapped right end.
Unresolved features must not be executed using placeholder parameters. The left end bevel and left shoulder radius remain provisional.
The .38 tapped depth is not a separately specified total drilling depth.

STAMP "SB-12010" on the main cylindrical surface is a manufacturing instruction. Text stamping is unsupported by the available Feature IR geometry types; character size, depth, orientation and precise location are unspecified.
